questions.prompt: Which one of these foods is unhealthy?
questions.explanation: Sweets are full of sugar and they are bad for your body and your teeth, so they belong to the unhealthy basket. Yoghurt, fish and bread are healthy food, and you should eat them every week.

questions.prompt: Your stomach hurts after a very big meal. Complete: "I have ___."
questions.explanation: The pain is in the stomach, and the name of that ailment ends in -ache: I have a stomachache. The word stomach alone names the part of the body, not the pain, and the two other ailments name a pain in the head and a pain in a tooth.

questions.prompt: Your friend wants to keep fit. Which piece of advice helps him?

options.text: You should play sport twice a week.
You should watch television all day.

questions.explanation: Playing sport twice a week is what keeps a body fit, so it is the good idea that should introduces. The advice to watch television all day works against a fit body, and the two sentences with shouldn't take away exactly what keeps him fit: sport and vegetables.

questions.prompt: The bottle in the kitchen is medicine, not juice. Complete: "You ___ drink it."
questions.explanation: Drinking someone else's medicine is dangerous, so it is forbidden, and what is forbidden takes mustn't: You mustn't drink it. The word must would make it necessary, should would make it a good idea, and can would say that you are able to do it and free to try.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Meriem did not sleep last night. She ___ very tired today."
questions.explanation: The word tired is an adjective, so it takes the verb to be, and with she that verb is is: She is very tired today. The verb have belongs to an ailment such as a headache, and are goes with you, we and they, never with she.

questions.prompt: You are making a salad. Which question about the oil is correct?

options.text: How much oil do you put in the salad?
How many oil do you put in the salad?
How much oils do you put in the salad?
How many oils do you put in the salad?

questions.explanation: Oil cannot be counted one by one, so it is an uncountable noun: it keeps no plural -s and it takes How much. The word How many belongs to nouns you can count, and adding an -s to oil tries to count what is not countable.
